hug-3-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-5-004.title: Preferred language in two settings
hug-3-5-004.description: The same 100 hypothetical traders report one preferred language in each setting. At home: R 60%, S 40%, L 0%. At the mixed-language market: R 10%, S 10%, L 80%.
hug-3-5-004.caption: Each setting totals100%; these are preferences, not a test of every language a person can speak. L is used for communication between different home-language groups.

hug-3-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-6-001.title: Message delivery between the same two cities
hug-3-6-001.description: Hypothetical cities remain 1,000 km apart. Message-delivery delays are 48 hours earlier, 6 hours in the middle observation, and 0.5 hours later. No change in physical distance is recorded.
hug-3-6-001.caption: Original synthetic communication-delay observations, not actual transport times or proof of equal household access. Stages are ordered observations, not equal calendar intervals.

hug-3-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-6-002.title: Local interactions and a wider media audience
hug-3-6-002.description: Hypothetical R and S districts interact at a city studio to create a performance, then an online feed shares it internationally.
hug-3-6-002.caption: Original schematic; arrows record documented interaction/sharing, not identical audience responses or migration counts.
hug-3-6-002.assumptions: Local contacts contribute to the performance; the online feed provides a subsequent international connection.

hug-3-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-6-003.title: Shared platform and language of posts
hug-3-6-003.description: Hypothetical countries A and B each have 90% platform P use among surveyed residents. Among their users’ R/S posts, A has 80% R and 20% S; B has 20% R and 80% S.
hug-3-6-003.caption: Platform use is a percentage of sampled residents; post languages are percentages of posts. These separate indicators must not be added as one exclusive total.

hug-3-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-6-004.title: Local-language uploads in equal periods
hug-3-6-004.description: Hypothetical local-language uploads total 5 earlier and 40 later during equal-length periods. Counts do not identify unique people.
hug-3-6-004.caption: Digital production is measured, not speaker totals, child acquisition or proficiency. No real language’s vitality statistics are represented.

hug-3-7-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-7-001.title: Movement and later adoption at Harbor
hug-3-7-001.description: Hypothetical families move east from Hearth to Harbor. After arrival, some nonmigrant Harbor residents adopt religion R through contact. Dates record a sequence, not measured travel time.
hug-3-7-001.caption: Original schematic; the arrow represents residential movement. Later local adoption is separately documented, not a second migration arrow. No real religion or geographic scale is represented.

hug-3-7-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-7-002.title: Three languages in a classification exercise
hug-3-7-002.description: In this hypothetical classroom exercise, an original table lists English as Indo-European/Germanic, Spanish as Indo-European/Romance, and Hindi as Indo-European/Indo-Aryan. These are factual classifications, not invented language relationships.
hug-3-7-002.caption: Original teaching representation of established classifications. The hypothetical exercise is not a speaker survey, complete family tree or map of present-day religions.

hug-3-7-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-7-003.title: Place-name origins and household language
hug-3-7-003.description: Hypothetical district: 70% of its recorded old place names derive from language L; 20% of currently surveyed households report L as their main home language.
hug-3-7-003.caption: Two separate percentages with separate denominators. Names and households are not interchangeable or exclusive categories; no actual district is depicted.

hug-3-7-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-7-004.title: One community’s membership ledger
hug-3-7-004.description: Hypothetical community begins with 100 adherents. It records 10 births within the community, 20 arriving adherents and 30 nonmigrant residents converting. No deaths or departures occur; final membership is 160.
hug-3-7-004.caption: Original synthetic accounting, not statistics for a real religion. Categories are distinct additions and count people once; it does not model every kind of religious change.

hug-3-8-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-8-001.title: Two practices in the same participant group
hug-3-8-001.description: Hypothetical repeated survey of the same 100 people. City-language use rises from 30 to 80; inherited-festival participation stays at 70. A person may report both practices.
hug-3-8-001.caption: Original synthetic paired-group totals. Measures are not mutually exclusive, and individual overlaps are not supplied. Counts do not establish every dimension of identity.

hug-3-8-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-8-002.title: Contributions to a new ceremony
hug-3-8-002.description: Hypothetical participants use a melody from tradition R and an instrument and rhythm from tradition S in one newly created ceremony.
hug-3-8-002.caption: Original schematic of documented contributions, not a claim that entire cultures merge or lose every distinction.
hug-3-8-002.assumptions: Both contributions are intentionally combined in one ceremony; arrows represent cultural inputs, not migration or population totals.

hug-3-8-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-8-003.title: Cultural centers and a shared school
hug-3-8-003.description: Hypothetical West and East districts each have a cultural center. Routes from both centers reach one shared public school. Cultural institutions are protected and school access is open to both groups.
hug-3-8-003.caption: Original schematic; paths represent available access, not compulsory attendance or residential separation. Cultural affiliation of every resident is not mapped.

hug-3-8-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-3-8-004.title: Home-language use across three cohorts
hug-3-8-004.description: Hypothetical descendant-generation cohorts: national-language home use is 50%, 85%, 95%; ancestral-language home use is 70%, 35%, 10%. Households may use both.
hug-3-8-004.caption: Original synthetic cross-sectional cohorts, not the same people tracked through time. Each percentage refers to households within its cohort; language measures can overlap.

hug-4-1-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-1-001.title: R settlements and two independent states
hug-4-1-001.description: Hypothetical independent states A and B share a north–south international boundary. Four settlements of the same self-identified nation R lie in A and four in B. Dots locate settlements, not equal population counts.
hug-4-1-001.caption: Original schematic. The map supplies national identification and state status; it does not map every resident, ethnic identity or an autonomous jurisdiction.

hug-4-1-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-1-002.title: Four hypothetical political entities
hug-4-1-002.description: Hypothetical entity A independently governs a territorial population. B is a province, C is a shared cultural community, and D is a voluntary association. Their external authority differs.
hug-4-1-002.caption: Original simplified classification exercise, not legal advice about disputed territories or a complete test of international recognition.
rows: External affairs held by larger state

hug-4-1-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-1-003.title: Reported national identities in State P
hug-4-1-003.description: Hypothetical survey of State P: 70% identify with nation R and 30% with nation S. For this exercise respondents choose one category; both are established national communities with distinct institutions inside the same independent state.
hug-4-1-003.caption: Original synthetic simplified categories, not a claim that national identity is always exclusive or can be inferred from appearance. A survey share does not determine sovereignty.

hug-4-1-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-1-004.title: An internal region within State P
hug-4-1-004.description: Hypothetical State P occupies the entire outer rectangle. Region R occupies the western part and governs specified local matters. P retains external affairs; the north–south internal line bounds R rather than a second independent state.
hug-4-1-004.caption: Original schematic of an autonomy arrangement. It does not assign identical powers to all real autonomous regions or map cultural boundaries.
hug-4-1-004.unitLabel: Entire rectangle: State P; inner line: regional boundary

hug-4-2-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-2-001.title: Three changes in K’s governing institutions
hug-4-2-001.description: Hypothetical timeline: 1920, an external power appoints a colonial governor; 1960, K becomes independent with domestic and external authority; 1990, K gives specified local powers to a regional legislature while retaining external affairs.
hug-4-2-001.caption: Original invented chronology, not a timeline for an actual state. A regional institution’s creation is distinguished from independent external statehood.

hug-4-2-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-2-002.title: Settlements and a boundary after independence
hug-4-2-002.description: Hypothetical A and B become independent on either side of a former internal colonial line at x=40. Settlements of self-identified nation R remain in their previous locations on both sides.
hug-4-2-002.caption: Original schematic of the post-independence arrangement. Dots locate R settlements rather than equal population totals; the prior colonial line is retained, not inferred from an unlabeled map.
hug-4-2-002.unitLabel: Dots: unchanged R settlements; line: inherited boundary

hug-4-2-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-2-003.title: Administration of ten specified policy fields
hug-4-2-003.description: Hypothetical state: regional bodies administer 4 fields earlier and 7 later; the central government administers 6 earlier and 3 later. The same ten fields are assigned once each. External affairs remain at state level.
hug-4-2-003.caption: Original synthetic allocation. A field count does not imply equal political importance, fiscal size or complete regional sovereignty. The state’s international boundary is unchanged.

hug-4-2-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-2-004.title: A hypothetical regional consultation
hug-4-2-004.description: Hypothetical consultation: 1,000 registered voters, 800 valid votes, 480 for autonomy and 320 for independence. The other 200 registered voters do not vote. No invalid ballots are recorded.
hug-4-2-004.caption: Original synthetic consultation. No legal threshold, binding consequence or preference of nonvoters is supplied. The result does not automatically create an independent state.

hug-4-3-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-3-001.title: A narrow channel on a shipping route
hug-4-3-001.description: Hypothetical ships use a 120-km channel route between West and East ports. If it closes, the specified alternative is 600 km. Both are traveled at 30 km/h; only the channel route is drawn.
hug-4-3-001.caption: Original schematic, not to scale; route distances are supplied assumptions, not measurements from the drawing. The alternative exists outside this view. No actual strait, current closure or real shipping data are represented.

hug-4-3-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-3-002.title: Institutions and leverage in a hypothetical agreement
hug-4-3-002.description: A hypothetical independent state retains its government and external status. A dominant external financier can withhold essential refinancing unless specified port and revenue policies are accepted; alternatives are severely constrained.
hug-4-3-002.caption: Original analytical scenario, not a claim about a real country, company or ordinary lending. The leverage is explicitly supplied; a foreign financial connection alone does not establish domination.

hug-4-3-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-3-003.title: Outside support and a regional contest
hug-4-3-003.description: Hypothetical rival powers P and Q support opposing factions R and S. The factions contest control of the same region. The model documents political relationships, not ethnic populations.
hug-4-3-003.caption: Original simplified schematic. Internal division and external competition are supplied together; no actual conflict or inevitable outcome is asserted.
hug-4-3-003.assumptions: P and Q are external rivals; R and S contest the same territory. Support arrows do not quantify aid or imply that factions lack local agency.

hug-4-3-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-3-004.title: Forest access permits before and after a concession
hug-4-3-004.description: Hypothetical forest permits: households hold 80 earlier and 20 later; a company holds 20 earlier and 80 later. The same 100 permits are allocated once each. The forest supports livelihoods and community ceremonies.
hug-4-3-004.caption: Original synthetic access counts. Permits are not people, consent votes or equal-value resource shares. The concession changes the authority for approving access; no legal ownership dispute is adjudicated.

hug-4-4-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-4-001.title: A border defined by a surveyed coordinate
hug-4-4-001.description: Hypothetical agreement places the border at straight survey coordinate x=50. Area A lies west and Area B east. No settlement chronology or cultural distribution is supplied.
hug-4-4-001.caption: Original planar survey schematic, not a real global projection. The given coordinate defines placement; map appearance alone does not establish the line’s historical origin.

hug-4-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-4-002.title: Boundary agreement and later town development
hug-4-4-002.description: Hypothetical timeline: earlier Indigenous land use is documented; in 1850 an active boundary is agreed; after 1900 the specified farming-town settlement pattern develops. The question compares the line with that later pattern.
hug-4-4-002.caption: Original invented chronology. Earlier land use is not erased or labeled culturally empty; antecedent is evaluated relative to the stated later landscape. The boundary remains active.

hug-4-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-4-003.title: A former dividing line in one current city
hug-4-4-003.description: Hypothetical city now forms one political jurisdiction. The former boundary at x=25 no longer governs territory, but parts of its wall alignment remain visible. The path marks that historical trace.
hug-4-4-003.caption: Original schematic. The whole rectangle is one present jurisdiction. A preserved trace is not a current international or administrative frontier.
hug-4-4-003.unitLabel: Path: former boundary trace; no current dividing function

hug-4-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-4-004.title: Reported cultural patterns in four districts
hug-4-4-004.description: Hypothetical districts report R shares: NW90%, NE20%, SW80%, SE10%; all other respondents select S. Negotiators later choose the western/eastern divide for a new border. Each district retains a minority share.
hug-4-4-004.caption: Original synthetic simplified identity survey, not actual ethnic territories. The north–south center line is the new border; horizontal lines only divide statistical districts. Reported identities are not inferred from appearance or biology.

hug-4-5-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-5-001.title: Four actions in one boundary agreement
hug-4-5-001.description: Hypothetical record: a treaty describes the agreed route; cartographers draw its course; survey teams install markers; officials operate a checkpoint under crossing rules.
hug-4-5-001.caption: Original invented sequence. Functions may overlap in real negotiations, but the recorded actions identify the specific task being compared.
rows: Write the agreed route in words

hug-4-5-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-5-002.title: Three supplied distances from a coastal baseline
hug-4-5-002.description: Hypothetical coastal baseline at the land–sea edge. Positions A, B and C are respectively 5, 50 and 210 nautical miles seaward from that baseline. The supplied distances, not the drawing’s spacing, determine zone membership.
hug-4-5-002.caption: Original not-to-scale diagram. The points are deliberately spread for readability. Assume a 12-nmi territorial sea and 200-nmi EEZ with no overlapping claims; extended continental-shelf questions are outside this exercise.
hug-4-5-002.unitLabel: Point labels give nautical miles from the baseline

hug-4-5-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-5-003.title: A transect between two opposite baselines
hug-4-5-003.description: Hypothetical opposite baselines A and B are 300 nautical miles apart along the horizontal transect. Each state proposes 200 nmi toward the other. A’s and B’s lands lie at the left and right edges.
hug-4-5-003.caption: Original simplified cross-sea geometry. Horizontal separation is supplied as 300 nmi; this is not a real coast, final maritime boundary or two-dimensional overlap-area calculation.

hug-4-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-5-004.title: Waiting at one unchanged crossing
hug-4-5-004.description: Hypothetical crossing waits under earlier and later rules: freight 20 then 50 minutes; commuters 10 then 40 minutes. The border and crossing location remain unchanged.
hug-4-5-004.caption: Original synthetic illustrative waits. Same measured categories, different administrative rules; no claim about an actual border or every cause of delay.

hug-4-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-6-001.title: R votes in nine equal-population precincts
hug-4-6-001.description: Hypothetical nine-cell grid, rows A B C; D E F; G H I. Each precinct has 100 residents, all casting one valid R-or-S ballot. R votes are 80 in A/B/C and 40 in every other cell. S receives the remaining votes.
hug-4-6-001.caption: Original simplified election, not actual voters or a legal districting template. Each row or column is contiguous and contains 300 residents. Colors encode votes, not identity; the question specifies the district grouping.
hug-4-6-001.unitLabel: R votes out of 100 valid votes per precinct

hug-4-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-6-002.title: Two plans using the same precincts
hug-4-6-002.description: Hypothetical row and column plans regroup the same 900 residents and ballots. Every district has 300 residents and valid votes; each elects one representative by simple majority.
hug-4-6-002.caption: Original synthetic totals computed from the nine-precinct example. Both plans are contiguous on the supplied grid. This comparison illustrates aggregation effects, not a finding about a real plan’s legality or intent.

hug-4-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-6-003.title: One vote share and two seat shares
hug-4-6-003.description: Hypothetical R vote share is 53.3% statewide. With the same votes, R wins 33.3% of seats under the row plan and 100% under the column plan. Values are rounded to one decimal where needed.
hug-4-6-003.caption: Original synthetic single-member election. Vote share uses 900 ballots; each seat share uses three seats. A mismatch is an outcome to investigate, not by itself proof of unlawful conduct or deliberate manipulation.

hug-4-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-6-004.title: R votes in four proposed districts
hug-4-6-004.description: Hypothetical proposed districts each contain 100 residents casting 100 valid R-or-S votes. R receives 90 in NW and 40 in NE, SW and SE; S receives the remainder. The planner’s stated aim is supplied in the question.
hug-4-6-004.caption: Original synthetic district totals. Equal population and simple shapes do not certify fairness; no actual electorate or legal finding is represented. One representative per district, simple majority, no ties.
hug-4-6-004.unitLabel: R votes out of 100 in each district

hug-4-7-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-7-001.title: Instructions and regional implementation
hug-4-7-001.description: Hypothetical national government sends instructions to West and East offices. Their powers are delegated by ordinary national law and can be withdrawn by that central authority.
hug-4-7-001.caption: Original simplified hierarchy. Arrows represent supplied authority relationships, not migration, votes or the structure of every unitary state.
hug-4-7-001.assumptions: Regional offices implement national decisions; no independently entrenched regional governing powers are supplied.

hug-4-7-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-7-002.title: Two sources of regional governing authority
hug-4-7-002.description: Hypothetical A delegates specified regional tasks through ordinary national law. B’s constitution allocates protected responsibilities to both national and regional governments; ordinary central legislation cannot simply abolish the regional level.
hug-4-7-002.caption: Original comparison of stated institutional rules, not legal advice about a real constitution. Both can have local offices, elected officials and different levels of service performance.
rows: Not permitted by ordinary law alone

hug-4-7-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-7-003.title: Regional household-recycling targets
hug-4-7-003.description: Hypothetical regional targets: NW 40%, NE 60%, SW 40%, SE 60% of households. The map does not say whether powers to set targets are constitutionally protected or delegated.
hug-4-7-003.caption: Original synthetic policy targets, not achieved outcomes. Regional difference alone does not classify federal/unitary structure or measure the success of either system.

hug-4-7-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-7-004.title: National and regional governing centers
hug-4-7-004.description: Hypothetical state has one national center N and four regional capitals W1, E1, W2 and E2. The constitution assigns regional institutions specified local responsibilities and national institutions other responsibilities.
hug-4-7-004.caption: Original schematic of locations, not proportional power symbols. Regional boundaries remain internal; constitutional responsibilities, not point size, explain the distributed centers.
hug-4-7-004.unitLabel: Points: governing centers within one state

hug-4-8-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-8-001.title: A ridge and access to national services
hug-4-8-001.description: Hypothetical single state: West and East are separated by a mountain ridge. The national capital is in West. East residents report difficult access to its services and seek more local decision-making; the figure shows a physical barrier, not an international border.
hug-4-8-001.caption: Original schematic; region lines identify physical areas within one state. No scale, real mountain range or necessary political outcome is represented.
hug-4-8-001.unitLabel: Ridge: physical barrier; all areas remain one state

hug-4-8-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-8-002.title: Two regions and a simplified central budget
hug-4-8-002.description: Hypothetical East and West each have 100,000 residents. East contributes 80 million currency units and receives 40 million in the recorded spending; West contributes 20 million and receives 60 million.
hug-4-8-002.caption: Original synthetic partial fiscal ledger. It does not capture every service, transfer, distributional goal or resident’s preference. A movement’s grievance is not itself proof of inevitable fragmentation.

hug-4-8-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-8-003.title: A claim across an existing state border
hug-4-8-003.description: Hypothetical State A lies west of the international border at x=40. Borderland R and the rest of B lie east, within State B. A’s government claims R on asserted national ties; the arrow records that claim, not a completed transfer.
hug-4-8-003.caption: Original schematic, not a real territorial claim. The line at x=65 only marks the claimed borderland’s extent inside B. No military movement, valid entitlement or political agreement is represented.
hug-4-8-003.unitLabel: Arrow: asserted incorporation claim, not migration

hug-4-8-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-8-004.title: Reported support for regional autonomy
hug-4-8-004.description: Hypothetical representative surveys: North support is 20% earlier and 55% later; South is 30% earlier and 35% later. Multiple political and economic changes occur between surveys. Different respondents may be sampled.
hug-4-8-004.caption: Original synthetic survey estimates with consistent regional populations and question wording. No sampling uncertainty is modeled; the chart alone does not identify a single cause, every individual’s change or support for independence.

hug-4-9-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-9-001.title: Examples of subnational territorial institutions
hug-4-9-001.description: In a hypothetical classroom comparison, factual examples include Spain’s autonomous communities, Belgium’s regions, Canada’s provinces and territories, and Nigeria’s states. Their powers and origins differ.
hug-4-9-001.caption: Original comparative representation, not invented country classifications. Belgium also has communities; Canadian provinces and territories differ constitutionally. The list is illustrative rather than an exhaustive institutional map.

hug-4-9-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-9-002.title: Several uses of a shared communication network
hug-4-9-002.description: Hypothetical digital network helps a regional campaign coordinate, a civic forum share information, and an international environmental project collaborate. The figure records uses rather than guaranteed political outcomes.
hug-4-9-002.caption: Original schematic; the same infrastructure can serve different scales and aims. No real platform, causal effect size or automatic constitutional change is represented.
hug-4-9-002.assumptions: Arrows mean facilitated communication. They do not establish that campaigns succeed or that every resident has equal access.

hug-4-9-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-9-003.title: A river connecting three states
hug-4-9-003.description: Hypothetical river flows east from A through B to C. A release near the upstream site can affect the downstream intake. The three areas are independent states with separate governing institutions.
hug-4-9-003.caption: Original schematic of physical connectivity, not a real pollution event or hydrological concentration model. Arrow direction, not the political colors, indicates flow.

hug-4-9-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-9-004.title: Selected organizations and broad roles
hug-4-9-004.description: Hypothetical classroom comparison using factual broad roles of six organizations. The list compares purposes and regions, not identical legal powers or guaranteed outcomes.
hug-4-9-004.caption: Original concise representation of institutional mandates. Organizations differ in decision rules and authority; these are not interchangeable world governments.

hug-4-10-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-10-001.title: Travel time to shared public services
hug-4-10-001.description: Hypothetical typical one-way travel time: Core 60 minutes earlier and 45 later; Periphery 180 earlier and 60 later. The service type and travel-time definition are held constant.
hug-4-10-001.caption: Original synthetic access measures. They do not directly measure trust, identity, equal service quality or political preferences; possible integration effects need additional evidence.

hug-4-10-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-10-002.title: Settlements with regular public-service presence
hug-4-10-002.description: Hypothetical districts each contain 100 settlements. Regular service presence: NW 90%, NE 80%, SW 20%, SE 10%. The North is NW+NE and South SW+SE; this is one defined service indicator.
hug-4-10-002.caption: Original synthetic territorial-coverage data. Settlement counts are equal; resident populations need not be. The map does not identify ethnicity, legal recognition, every service or security control.

hug-4-10-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-10-003.title: Reported inclusion in two respondent groups
hug-4-10-003.description: Hypothetical surveys sample 100 M respondents and 100 N respondents at each observation. Those reporting that the national campaign includes their group: M 90 earlier/95 later; N 30 earlier/10 later. Samples are not population weights or necessarily the same individuals.
hug-4-10-003.caption: Original synthetic responses. The campaign’s content is supplied in the question; the table alone does not establish causation, every person’s response or the groups’ share of the state population.

hug-4-10-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-4-10-004.title: R settlements after a hypothetical breakup
hug-4-10-004.description: Hypothetical former state X fragments into independent A, B and C. The same self-identified nation R has two marked settlements in each. None of the successors constitutes an independent state of R; the dots do not imply migration.
hug-4-10-004.caption: Original schematic of a supplied political outcome. Dots locate settlements rather than equal populations. Not every breakup produces this outcome, and individual citizenship is not mapped.
hug-4-10-004.unitLabel: Dots: settlements of nation R; lines: successor-state borders

hug-5-1-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-1-001.title: Seasonal rainfall at a mild-winter farm
hug-5-1-001.description: Hypothetical seasonal rainfall totals: winter 300 mm, spring 180, summer 20 and autumn 200. Winters are mild. Seasons refer to the local annual cycle, not fixed months shared across hemispheres.
hug-5-1-001.caption: Original synthetic rainfall totals, not observations from a named farm. Rainfall timing influences choices alongside soils, water access, technology, labor and markets; no particular irrigation supply is assumed.

hug-5-1-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-1-002.title: Farm area and annual labor inputs
hug-5-1-002.description: Hypothetical farms: A uses 3000 labor hours on 10 hectares, B 10000 on 1000 hectares, and C 8000 on 100 hectares. Hours use the same annual definition for all farms.
hug-5-1-002.caption: Original synthetic inputs. Farm size, total hours, labor per hectare and labor per worker are different measures. Capital, output prices and profitability are not supplied.

hug-5-1-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-1-003.title: One seasonal grazing movement
hug-5-1-003.description: Hypothetical herders move animals from a wet-season grazing area toward a dry-season water location, using broad rangelands. The arrow shows one seasonal leg, not a permanent residential move or a full annual cycle.
hug-5-1-003.caption: Original schematic of resource access, not actual customary land, a state border or a recommended route. Irregular areas identify physical grazing zones; no geographic scale is given.

hug-5-1-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-1-004.title: An evenly staggered cultivation cycle
hug-5-1-004.description: Hypothetical equal-area plots rotate through 2 cropped years and 6 fallow years. Phases are evenly staggered across the system, so each cycle position occupies an equal share of its total land.
hug-5-1-004.caption: Original simplified rotation, not an instruction to clear land or a universal fallow recommendation. Fallow vegetation and soil recovery are part of the system; actual sustainable timing varies.

hug-5-2-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-2-001.title: Households near one farming hamlet
hug-5-2-001.description: Hypothetical nine farmhouses form a compact cluster near the right side of the mapped farming area. Households cultivate fields beyond the residential cluster; dots locate homes rather than population totals.
hug-5-2-001.caption: Original schematic of residences and fields, not a real village or ownership map. A settlement pattern does not by itself identify its historical cause, crop system or survey method.

hug-5-2-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-2-002.title: Long lots and homes near a river
hug-5-2-002.description: Hypothetical four narrow lots extend inland from the same river frontage. Each contains one house near the bank; the four homes align parallel to the river. Lot labels identify parcels, not independent jurisdictions.
hug-5-2-002.caption: Original parcel/residence schematic, not to scale. Each lot reaches the river at its southern end. A straight row is visible, but a real historical survey requires records beyond appearance.

hug-5-2-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-2-003.title: Six cells from a larger rectangular survey
hug-5-2-003.description: Hypothetical partial survey grid with six adjacent cells, A–F. Accompanying records cite a principal meridian, baseline, townships and sections. This is not a whole township or a real survey plat.
hug-5-2-003.caption: Original schematic. Standard PLSS townships nominally contain 36 sections; actual surveys and corrections vary. This small excerpt shows a regular pattern without reproducing official section numbering or legal boundaries.

hug-5-2-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-2-004.title: A parcel and referenced corner features
hug-5-2-004.description: Hypothetical parcel corners P,Q,R,S,T form an irregular outline. A deed starts at stone P, records bearings/distances for courses, and uses the creek from R to S as one referenced feature. The drawing does not supply actual legal measurements.
hug-5-2-004.caption: Original schematic of supplied deed references. Shape alone does not identify a survey method, and this is not a legal description, navigation instruction or real property claim.
hug-5-2-004.unitLabel: Letters: deed corners; path: creek reference

hug-5-3-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-3-001.title: Selected early agricultural hearth regions
hug-5-3-001.description: Hypothetical classroom map with original simplified continental outlines. A is in Mesoamerica/Central America; B in Southwest Asia; C in the Indus region of South Asia; D in Southeast Asia. Markers locate broad regions, not excavation sites.
hug-5-3-001.caption: Original outline sketch on a simplified longitude/latitude grid from 80°N to 60°S; not a complete coastline, political-boundary or distance map. The selected hearths are not an exhaustive list of independent domestication centers.

hug-5-3-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-3-002.title: Two crop movements in the Columbian Exchange
hug-5-3-002.description: Hypothetical simplified Atlantic-centered diagram. A maize arrow runs from the Americas on the left toward Afro-Eurasia on the right. A wheat arrow runs in the opposite direction. These represent post 1492 transfers rather than measured volumes.
hug-5-3-002.caption: Original regional sketch; arrow widths and routes are illustrative. Only two crop movements are shown, not the full Columbian Exchange or its unequal social consequences.

hug-5-3-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-3-003.title: Evidence for a hypothetical crop lineage
hug-5-3-003.description: Hypothetical archaeological exercise, not real excavations or dates. Samples at each site are securely identified and dated; later domesticated samples belong to the same distinctive inherited lineage as P.
hug-5-3-003.caption: Years before present increase backward in time. Missing or undiscovered evidence could change an origin hypothesis; a modern harvest ranking would not supply equivalent historical evidence.
rows: Related wild plants and early selection evidence

hug-5-3-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-3-004.title: Spread of an introduced crop in two districts
hug-5-3-004.description: Hypothetical survey of farms adopting the same introduced domesticated seed. Frequent-contact district:5%,40%,80%; limited-contact district:5%,10%,20% at years 0,10,20. Both have comparable rainfall and soils.
hug-5-3-004.caption: Original synthetic adoption percentages. Years are equally spaced; farm costs, preferences and other possible differences are not fully controlled.

hug-5-4-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-001.title: Farm output, land and labor before and after changes
hug-5-4-001.description: Hypothetical same-region annual crop totals before and after improved farming methods. Crop output rises from 600 to 900 tonnes; cultivated land remains 300 hectares; agricultural workers fall from 60 to 30.
hug-5-4-001.caption: Original synthetic comparison, not measured historical data. Output per worker and output per hectare use different denominators; the table does not identify every cause of the changes.

hug-5-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-002.title: Food output and population indices
hug-5-4-002.description: Hypothetical region. Initially food output and population both have index 100. Later the food-output index is 150 and the population index 125. Each series uses its own initial value as the base.
hug-5-4-002.caption: Original synthetic indices, not quantities in tonnes or numbers of people. The ratio measures a relative aggregate output-per-person change, not access or diet quality.

hug-5-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-003.title: Scattered strips and consolidated holdings
hug-5-4-003.description: Hypothetical paired parcel sketch. Left, before: six alternating narrow strips labeled A1,B1,A2,B2,A3,B3. Right, after: one contiguous block A and one contiguous block B. A and B denote the same two holders in both panels.
hug-5-4-003.caption: Original schematic of spatial consolidation, not a real enclosure award. Before is on the left and after on the right. Equal schematic areas do not document historic compensation, common rights or household migration.
hug-5-4-003.unitLabel: Left: before; right: after. Letters identify holders.

hug-5-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-004.title: Matched planting-method trial
hug-5-4-004.description: Hypothetical matched plots of the same crop under the same soil and weather conditions. Broadcasting scatters 1000 viable seeds, with 600 plants established and 2.4 tonnes/hectare yield. Drill rows place 1000 seeds, with 800 plants established and 3.0 tonnes/hectare yield.
hug-5-4-004.caption: Original synthetic controlled comparison for understanding planting technology. A seed drill places seed in rows at regulated spacing/depth; actual outcomes vary with equipment, management and environment.
